title: International AI Safety Institute Landscape: Comparing Mandates and Outputs

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: a descriptive mapping of the global institute landscape informs coordination efforts but does not directly drive safety improvements. Useful reference material.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: coding 10+ institutes across multiple dimensions (mandate, budget, publications, methodology) requires systematic research skills and some governance domain knowledge.

narrow_scope.reasoning: No clear milestone: a comprehensive landscape analysis of 10+ countries is too broad for 30 hours. Would likely be incomplete or overly surface-level.

novelty.reasoning: This landscape mapping is substantially covered by existing work. All Tech Is Human published 'The Global Landscape of AI Safety Institutes' categorizing institutes as established, announced/in development, or network members. The OECD published 'AI Safety Institutes: Can countries meet the challenge?' comparing mandates and budgets. CSIS published 'The AI Safety Institute International Network: Next Steps and Recommendations.' The Stanford 2025 AI Index Report covers policy and governance including safety institutes. The International AI Safety Report 2025 and 2026 (internationalaisafetyreport.org) provide comprehensive cross-country analysis. Budget comparisons (UK ~$65M, US ~$48M, Canada ~C$50M) are publicly available. The core descriptive mapping proposed is already done by multiple organizations.
